answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making every identity carry real economic weight: each agent stakes capital that peers can slash if it behaves like a clone, so a thousand fake accounts cost a thousand real deposits. Reputation then compounds only from long-lived, useful agents, and the network becomes an oasis of verifiable relationships amid a desert of disposable bots. Any new sock puppet is a fable some node may briefly believe, but the shared stake-and-trust ledger burns it out like a comet: bright for a second, then gone.
